[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) in Machine Learning"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) is a critical initial step in the machine learning pipeline. It involves investigating datasets to summarize their main characteristics, often utilizing data visualization methods and descriptive statistics. A thorough EDA helps data scientists uncover patterns, spot anomalies, test hypotheses, and check assumptions before building complex models."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Importing Libraries and Loading Data"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The first step in any EDA workflow is loading your dataset into a structured format using Python libraries such as Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and Seaborn."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load dataset
df = pd.read_csv('dataset.csv')
print(df.head())"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Inspecting Data Structure and Types"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before diving into deep analysis, you need to understand the dimensions of your dataset, data types of each column, and the presence of any missing values."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# Check dataset dimensions
print("Shape:", df.shape)

# Check data types and non-null counts
print(df.info())"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"df.shape reveals the number of rows and columns."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"df.info() highlights memory usage and data types, helping identify numeric vs. categorical features."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Handling Missing Values"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Missing data can severely degrade machine learning model performance. Quantifying missing values early allows you to decide whether to impute or drop them."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"# Calculate sum of missing values per column
missing_values = df.isnull().sum()
print(missing_values[missing_values > 0])"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Statistical Summary"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Generating descriptive statistics provides a quick overview of central tendencies, dispersion, and shape of the dataset's numerical distributions."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"# Summary statistics for numerical features
print(df.describe())"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Data Visualization"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Visualizations translate raw numbers into intuitive insights. Univariate and bivariate plots help identify distributions, outliers, and correlations."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"# Plotting a correlation heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.heatmap(df.corr(), annot=True, cmap='coolwarm', fmt='.2f')
plt.title('Feature Correlation Heatmap')
plt.show()"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Histograms and Boxplots are ideal for detecting outliers in numerical features."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Countplots and Bar charts are useful for analyzing the frequency distribution of categorical variables."},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"Exploratory Data Analysis bridges the gap between raw data collection and feature engineering. By carefully executing these EDA steps, you ensure that your machine learning models are trained on clean, well-understood, and highly relevant features."}]
